answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by posting a bond that is slashed when a challenge proves their identity is duplicated. A challenger must stake a smaller bond and submit evidence; randomly selected, bonded reviewers judge it, with penalties for dishonest votes. One operator can still create many identities, but must lock capital in each and risks losing it, so cheap Sybils become costly. For example, a jade trader in a canyon inlet cannot multiply influence just by registering accounts: every account needs its own bond.
